Every song here stops two bars short. The chords for those bars are already written in: **V**, then **I** (or **i** in a minor key).
That's an authentic cadence, the strongest way to end. Your job is to write the melody that goes over it.

## Pick a song

```{=html}
<div id="we-pick" class="we-pick"><span class="we-note">Loading the tune library...</span></div>
<div class="we-paper" id="we-orig"></div>
<div class="we-tools">
  <button type="button" class="btn btn-outline-secondary" id="we-play-orig">&#9654; Hear it as written</button>
  <span class="we-note">The last two bars are silent. Only the chords play there.</span>
</div>
```

## What makes an ending sound finished

- **Land on the tonic.** End on the home note (D in these songs) on a strong beat. Make it long.
- **Over V, sit on the leading tone or the 2nd.** In D, that's C♯ or E. Over A, both pull you home to D.
- **Step down into the last note.** 3–2–1 (F♯–E–D) or 2–1 sounds settled. A leap up to the tonic sounds bolder.
- **Echo the opening.** Bar 5 already repeats bar 1. Let your bars 7–8 answer bar 6 the way bars 3–4 answered bar 2.
- **Slow down.** Use longer notes in the last bar than in the rest of the song.

## Write it

The chords are already in place. Choose rhythm patterns: they fill the empty bars in order, and once the last bar is full
the song is complete (no bar is added). Then choose how to enter the notes (letters, the computer keys, or a MIDI keyboard)
and enter them; they fill the rhythm from the first empty note. The score above the tools shows your ending as you go.
Your work is saved for each song.

## Compare

Write two different endings for the same song. Write one that steps down 3–2–1 and one that leaps up to the tonic.
Then play them back to back. Which sounds more final? Which sounds more like *this* song?

```{=html}
<script src="/apps/shared/soundfont.js?v=1"></script>
<script src="/apps/shared/abcjs-basic.js?v=3"></script>
<script src="/apps/shared/abc-play.js?v=17"></script>
<script src="/apps/tunes/tunes-object.js?v=2"></script>
<script src="/apps/shared/lessons/sections.js?v=2"></script>
<script>
(function () {
  "use strict";
  var $ = function (id) { return document.getElementById(id); };
  var KEY = "ending:", frame = $("we-frame"), ready = false, cur = null, songs = [];

  // every tune in the library tagged %%id unfinished-song-N, wherever it lives: new ones, and edits to these, show up here
  Object.keys(tunesObject).forEach(function (c) {
    String(tunesObject[c]).split(/\n(?=X:)/).forEach(function (t) {
      var m = /%%id\s+(unfinished-song-\S+)/.exec(t);
      if (m) songs.push({ id: m[1], abc: t.trim(), title: (/^T:(.*)$/m.exec(t) || [, m[1]])[1].trim() });
    });
  });
  songs.sort(function (a, b) { return a.id.localeCompare(b.id, undefined, { numeric: true }); });

  function mine(s) { try { return localStorage.getItem(KEY + s.id); } catch (e) { return null; } }
  function draw(el, abc) { return ABCJS.renderAbc(el, abc, { responsive: "resize", add_classes: true })[0]; }

  var synth = null;
  function play(abc) {   // the band's samples (AbcPlay): the tune, and its chords on piano and bass when it has them
    if (synth) { synth.stop(); synth = null; }
    var tmp = document.createElement("div"), vo = ABCJS.renderAbc(tmp, abc)[0];
    synth = AbcPlay.play(vo, { light: false, abc: abc, drums: false });
  }

  function send() {
    if (!ready || !cur) return;
    frame.contentWindow.postMessage({ type: "end-load", abc: mine(cur) || cur.abc, title: cur.title }, location.origin);
  }
  function choose(s) {
    cur = s;
    Array.prototype.forEach.call($("we-pick").children, function (b) { b.classList.toggle("we-on", b.dataset.id === s.id); });
    draw($("we-orig"), s.abc);
    var m = mine(s); draw($("we-mine"), m || s.abc);
    $("we-msg").textContent = m ? "Your ending so far is below." : "";
    try { localStorage.setItem(KEY + "current", s.id); } catch (e) {}
    send();
  }

  $("we-pick").innerHTML = "";
  if (!songs.length) $("we-pick").innerHTML = '<span class="we-note">No unfinished songs in the tune library.</span>';
  songs.forEach(function (s) {
    var b = document.createElement("button");
    b.type = "button"; b.className = "btn btn-outline-secondary"; b.textContent = s.title; b.dataset.id = s.id;
    b.onclick = function () { choose(s); };
    $("we-pick").appendChild(b);
  });

  window.addEventListener("message", function (e) {
    if (e.source !== frame.contentWindow || e.origin !== location.origin || !e.data) return;
    if (e.data.type === "end-ready") { ready = true; send(); }
    if (e.data.type === "end-change" && cur && typeof e.data.abc === "string") {
      try { localStorage.setItem(KEY + cur.id, e.data.abc); } catch (err) {}
      draw($("we-mine"), e.data.abc);
    }
  });
  // the framed page grows with what's open in it
  setInterval(function () {
    try { var h = frame.contentDocument.documentElement.scrollHeight; if (h && Math.abs(h - frame.offsetHeight) > 20) frame.style.height = h + "px"; } catch (e) {}
  }, 700);

  $("we-play-orig").onclick = function () { if (cur) play(cur.abc); };
  $("we-play-mine").onclick = function () { if (cur) play(mine(cur) || cur.abc); };
  $("we-reset").onclick = function () {
    if (!cur || !confirm("Throw away your ending for " + cur.title + "?")) return;
    try { localStorage.removeItem(KEY + cur.id); } catch (e) {}
    choose(cur);
  };

  var last = null; try { last = localStorage.getItem(KEY + "current"); } catch (e) {}
  if (songs.length) choose(songs.find(function (s) { return s.id === last; }) || songs[0]);
})();
</script>
```

Caplin, William E. *Classical Form: A Theory of Formal Functions for the Instrumental Music of Haydn, Mozart, and Beethoven*. Oxford UP, 1998. Caplin reads most textbook plagal cadences as postcadential codettas (confirmed from secondary summaries, not the book itself).

Gould, Elaine. *Behind Bars: The Definitive Guide to Music Notation*. Faber Music, 2011. Grace notes, trills and other ornaments in modern notation.

Walshaw, Chris, editor. "The abc Music Standard 2.1." *abcnotation.com*, 2011. [abcnotation.com/wiki/abc:standard:v2.1](https://abcnotation.com/wiki/abc:standard:v2.1).
